newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo says in talks with EU on Lonrho link.
newsitem.headline: Anglo says in talks with EU on Lonrho link.

text.p: Mining giant Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Monday it was in talks with the European Union over a tie-up with Britain's Lonrho Plc conglomerate.
"We are in ongoing discussions," an Anglo spokesman told Reuters.
Britain's Independent on Sunday newspaper had reported that the European Commission was investigating the deal with Lonrho over concerns about reduced competition in the platinum market.
The spokesman said Anglo was confident it could deal with the EC's worries, but could not give a time-scale for the talks to be completed.
"We are confident...but the EU is in the driving seat on this (time-scale)," an Anglo spokesman said.

Anglo recently swelled its stake in Lonrho to a direct 25.9 and indirect 2.2 percent stake, making it the largest shareholder by far and effectively giving it control of the British group and its assets, including Lonrho Platinum.

In April this year the European Commission blocked a merger between Impala Platinum Holdings and Lonrho's platinum mines because it was seen as anti-trust with the new company holding 28 percent of the world platinum market.

Seizing its chance then, the EC warned Anglo against taking control of Lonrho, saying it would pose the same problem because Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd already holds 35 percent of the world's platinum market.
